subject.title: fix(cron): respect deliveryBestEffort in interim-message suppression guard

question: Should `deliveryBestEffort` bypass interim suppression only for a proven stale-descendant state, while continuing to suppress messages whenever descendant work is genuinely active?
rationale: The final patch changes an existing best-effort delivery policy for active descendants, but the claimed inactive stale-state path is not shown to reach the changed predicate; selecting the intended delivery contract requires owner intent.

options.title: Prove and narrow the stale-state repair
options.body: Keep active-descendant suppression, reproduce the exact inactive stale-state condition on current main, and patch only the reachable stale-state branch.

options.title: Treat best-effort as deliver-immediately
options.body: Restore delivery for active descendants too and document that best-effort intentionally permits interim output while child work continues.

options.title: Retain current suppression
options.body: Keep interim suppression for all descendant states and close this PR if the linked report cannot be reproduced on a current release.

recommendation.title: Prove and narrow the stale-state repair
recommendation.body: Keep active-descendant suppression, reproduce the exact inactive stale-state condition on current main, and patch only the reachable stale-state branch.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the descendant-gating behavior whose intended delivery semantics the PR changes.
